labels.label: bbsdef:circle_data_point_structure

hypotheses.paper: p a point of HS^2 (l.762, l.767)
hypotheses.note: field pt : GX.HS 2 (T-bbs-hs-model's HS^2, the rays of Causal.Minkowski 2)

hypotheses.paper: l(p), the space of rays in T_p HS^2 (l.762)
hypotheses.note: GX.Link p = GX.RaySphere (GX.TpHS p), TpHS p = R^{1,2}/Rp: the tangent plane of the ray space at [p]. The identification of the tangent plane with V/Rp depends on the representative p only through a positive scaling, which does not move rays, so the space of rays is canonical. A representation, disclosed in SCOPE (a), not a reading.

hypotheses.paper: Gamma_p, the pointwise stabiliser of p in SO_0(1,2), 'the subgroup which preserves every point of the ray p' (l.763-764)
hypotheses.note: GX.GammaP p = {A in Causal.Flat.lorentz 2 | A p = p}; GX.mem_gammaP_iff_ray: equivalently A (c p) = c p for every c > 0.

hypotheses.paper: the action of Gamma_p on l(p) (implicit)
hypotheses.note: the tangent action: A acts on R^{1,2}/Rp by the induced map (GX.GammaP.tangent, a linear equivalence) and on its rays by GX.linRaySmul; a MulAction with ContinuousConstSMul.

gx's convention (DEC-16): fields atlas : ChartedSpace (Link pt) L and hasGroupoid : HasGroupoid L (gxGroupoid (GammaP pt) (Link pt)), read over the maximal atlas. That (Gamma_p, l(p)) is analytic (faithful and rigid) is not proved and not needed by the definition.
field isCircle : GX.IsCircle L, i.e. L is homeomorphic to mathlib's Circle. l(p) itself is one: GX.GammaLinkCircle.regular (the link of a regular point).

findings: No statement of colI_v1.tex l.673-771 was found false. The next sentence (l.770-771, no label) is proved under the double-cover reading of its 'natural RP1-structure' (SCOPE (e); see the questions). GX.GammaLinkCircle.rp1_hasGroupoid gives every (Gamma_p, l(p))-circle an underlying RP1-structure. GX.GammaLinkCircle.rp1_compatible with GX.linkToRP1_eq_smul shows that it does not depend on the oriented identification of T_p HS^2 with R^2. These are listed under extra_decls, not as this label's declarations.
questions: The natural RP1-structure of l(p) (l.770), a reading disclosed in SCOPE (e). Reading taken: the double covering S(T_p HS^2) -> P(T_p HS^2) ~ RP1, read through an oriented identification T_p HS^2 = C (GX.linkToRP1, GX.IsOrientedTangent). Gamma_p acts through SL(2,R), because the determinant of its tangent action is det A = 1 (GX.det_tangent). Evidence that this is BBS's structure: at l.902-905 one turn of l(p) is delta^2, and here l(p) has lifted holonomy delta^2 (GX.hasLiftedHolonomy_link). It is the only reading uniform in p. At a space-like or light-like p, Gamma_p fixes four or two rays of l(p), and a non-trivial element of PSL(2,R) fixes at most two points of RP1 (a parabolic one only one), so no degree-one equivariant identification exists [r, also checked by the audit]. At a time-like p the visual map is a degree-one alternative: see the angle-normalisation question.

The orientation convention (l.621, l.770, and the fixed homeomorphism RP1~ = R of l.676-677) changes no invariant of the underlying RP1-circle. Convention taken: HS^2 is oriented as the unit sphere of R^{1,2} in the coordinates (t, x0, x1), outward normal first (GX.vol3, GX.IsOrientedTangent). RP1 = P(R^2) is oriented counterclockwise, and RP1~ = R through t -> [cos pi t : sin pi t]. The opposite orientation of HS^2, or of RP1~, gives the mirror RP1-structure, and the canonical orientation of l.729-731 flips with it. The new lifted holonomy is c~ f^-1 c~ = delta^k (c~ g^-1 c~), with c~ x = -x, and I^+- becomes -I^+-. Since g'(-x) >= -x iff g x >= x, the degree, the trace class, the angle and the sign (positive or negative, l.908-922) are unchanged; this invariance is not formalized. So the question is only which convention the author wants recorded.

dispatch_scope.note: An RP1-circle is [ChartedSpace RP1 L] [HasGroupoid L (gxGroupoid PSL(2,R) RP1)] with IsCircle L. PSL(2,R) is mathlib's Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup acting projectively. The action is faithful and rigid, and the centre is trivial. The classification of RP1-circles (l.701-760) is not formalized, apart from the degree and its sign.

G~ is 'the group of projective transformations of RP1~' (l.679-680): the lifts through RP1.proj of the elements of PSL(2,R), a subgroup of CircleDeg1Lift units. Proved: the exact sequence 0 -> Z -> G~ -> G -> 0, delta x > x, the centre of G~ is <delta>, and RP1~/Z = RP1. Elliptic elements act freely and properly discontinuously. Non-elliptic elements decompose as delta^k g with g fixing a point, and k is unique. Not formalized: that G~ is the universal covering group (no topology on either group), and that elliptic elements are conjugate to translations.

dispatch_scope.item: the real angle of an elliptic RP1-circle (l.742-744)
dispatch_scope.status: proved (well defined), under the normalisation reading
dispatch_scope.note: The lifted holonomy of an RP1-circle is f in G~ with D(s+1) = f(D s). Here D : R -> RP1~ is an increasing lift of a developing map along a periodic covering R -> L, and the increasing condition is the canonical orientation of l.729-731. Then f x > x at every point D s of the image (eq>, GX.lt_apply_of_strictMono). It exists, by gx's exists_developingMap on the pulled-back structure. It is unique up to conjugacy in G~. So the real angle 2 pi tau(f) is well defined. It is >= 0, and > 0 for elliptic or central holonomy. The degree k is >= 0 (l.740), and the angle of delta^k g is 2 pi k. RP1 itself has holonomy delta and angle 2 pi. l(p), with the double-cover structure of l.770 (SCOPE (e)), has holonomy delta^2 and angle 4 pi.

questions: Normalisation of 'the angle'. l.742-744 do not fix it, but the paper does: in Lemma surgery-key (l.2952-2969), 'C_+ carries an elliptic structure of angle theta' embeds e(Sigma) in P_theta, the model of a particle of cone angle theta (l.2827, the massive particle of l.1142-1159). In the regular case theta = 2 pi, C_+ = boundary of H^2 = RP1 with holonomy delta, so angle(delta) = 2 pi. This is the convention taken here (2 pi times the translation number of the lifted holonomy), and NOTES-3+1 N4's. Under the double-cover structure of l.770 (SCOPE (e)), the link of a regular point then has real angle 4 pi, not 2 pi (proved: GX.hasRealAngle_link, holonomy delta^2). The session's own reasoning [r], not evidence: the link of a cone point of cone angle theta has RP1-angle 2 theta, while a photon circle around that single cone point (N4/Lemma F, a = 1) has angle theta. The paper is not contradicted, since it only says time-like singularities are characterized by their elliptic RP1-circle (l.808-809) and by their cone angle (l.864). At a time-like p there is a second natural RP1-structure on l(p), Gamma_p-equivariant and of degree one. It is the visual map v -> endpoint of c_v on dH^2_+ ~ RP1, through SO_0(1,2) ~ PSL(2,R) (l.763). Under it a regular link has holonomy delta and angle 2 pi, and a cone point's link has angle equal to its cone angle. It does not exist at space-like or light-like p (SCOPE (e)). So the factor 2 can be removed in three ways. (i) Keep the uniform double cover, with angle(link) = 2 x cone angle: the formalized reading. (ii) Read l.770 at time-like p as the visual structure, a reading that depends on p. (iii) Renormalise delta = pi, which conflicts with surgery-key, as the photon circle of H^2 would then have angle pi. Which does the author intend? It matters for Theorem M's Theta and for Lemma F (F4), 0 < Theta < 2 pi.

'Elliptic' for G~ and for RP1-circles (l.688-694). Reading taken: GX.PSL2.IsElliptic is |tr| < 2, which excludes 1. The 'elliptic circles' include those with central holonomy delta^k, because l.693-694 includes RP1 itself, of holonomy delta, whose projection 1 is not elliptic. GX.HasRealAngle.pos_of_isElliptic therefore takes 'elliptic or central'.
See the label's questions for the double-cover reading of l.770 (SCOPE (e)) and for the orientation convention, which changes no invariant.
kb_proposals: RP1 is GX.RP1 = mathlib's Circle, the line R z being z / conj z (GX.RP1.mk, mk_eq_mk_iff). PSL(2,R) is mathlib's PSL(2, R), with GX.pslMk g . mk z = mk (slLin g z). The pair is analytic (GX.isAnalyticAction_rp1, via GX.eq_smul_of_eventually_eigen).

G~ is GX.GTilde, a subgroup of CircleDeg1Lift units: the lifts through RP1.proj t = exp(2 pi i t), so delta = t -> t + 1. Its real angle is 2 pi times mathlib's translationNumber (GX.GTilde.angle). Reuse translationNumber_conj_eq, translationNumber_mul_of_commute and lt_translationNumber_of_forall_add_lt.

Every lift of g in SL(2,R) to R commutes with t -> t + 1. The degree is a homomorphism to {1, -1}, trivial on squares, and SL(2,R) is a product of unipotents (GX.slDeg_eq_one, GX.sl_eq_upper_lower_upper). No connectedness of SL(2,R) is needed.

The holonomy of an RP1-circle lifted to G~ is GX.HasLiftedHolonomy: a periodic covering E : R -> L and an increasing lift D : R -> R of a developing map along E (GX.IsDevAlong). Existence: gx's exists_developingMap on pullbackChartedSpace (GX.isDevAlong_iff_isGXMorphism). Uniqueness up to conjugacy: GX.HasLiftedHolonomy.conj.

Change of model along an equivariant map q : X -> Y: GX.hasGroupoid_comp_of_equivariant puts an (H, Y)-structure on a (G, X)-manifold through ChartedSpace.comp, when every Y-chart of X is q (for instance a pullbackChartedSpace).

T_p HS^2 is Causal.Minkowski 2 quotiented by R . p. Its normed structure needs the local instance GX.isClosed_span_hs. The determinant of a map on the quotient comes from mathlib's LinearMap.det_eq_det_mul_det.
